# User-visible strings

**Generated by `npm run strings` — do not edit.** The source of truth is
`packages/capture-extension/public/_locales/en/messages.json`.

Every string a person can see, grouped by where it appears rather than by where it lives
in the code, because the reviewer is reading the popup and not the codebase.

Two rules apply to all of it (CONTRIBUTING.md, Rule 1):

1. The website is never the subject of a verb about intent. Enforced by `npm run lint:wording`.
2. An absence we observed and an absence we could not look for are different claims and
   must not share a phrase.

506 strings. 89 take placeholders.

## Toolbar icon

*Hover title of the extension's toolbar icon. The icon is blue when a GPC signal was observed on the page, whoever set it, and gray otherwise. Before a page reports, it shows this extension's setting; a badge reading ! with the last title means the browser did not install the header rule.*

| `actionTitleSending` | GPC Inspector: GPC signal on |  |
| `actionTitleOn` | GPC Inspector: GPC signal set on this page |  |
| `actionTitleOff` | GPC Inspector: no GPC signal on this page |  |
| `actionTitleRuleFailed` | GPC Inspector: cannot set the signal in this browser version |  |

## What this site did

*Key/value rows: how the site responded to GPC, and nothing else; GPP, USP and TCF have their own section. Every row leads with yes/no, every value distinguishes an absence we observed from one we could not look for, and 'checking' is its own state so a row never goes missing while a check is in flight. The GPC read rows come last, nested under the heading 'Read GPC from the page': 'Vendors seen reading GPC', 'Vendors with no read observed' and, when someone is in that state, 'Vendors that cannot be determined', each naming its vendors under the label or saying 'none', then the page's other facts in hint tone under the row they are about, and the GPP-string notes at the bottom of the group; the read count is not shown. A vendor is a company with its category, every one is listed, and scripts that belong to no vendor are named by domain.*

## Privacy strings — the expanded decode

*Field name, decoded meaning, raw encoded value. The third column is the point: IAB encodes 0 = not applicable, 1 = opted out, 2 = did NOT opt out, so the integer reverses the intuitive reading rather than merely failing to inform it and must never appear alone. Registry names (section ids, TCF purposes) are IAB's published wording and are deliberately untranslated — a paraphrase would change what the CMP said.*

*Per-vendor rows: the GPC check tag, plus USP/TCF secondary lines shown only when that specific API was called and attributed to the vendor. The engine has five check states; the 'this vendor checked' one splits into four tags here, because a check can be a GPP call or a direct read of the GPC property, and for a GPP call what the returned string recorded changes what can honestly be said about it.*

## Tag containers (below the vendors)

*The site's tag containers: one row per container, every Google tag id on one row, in the vendor row's markup. A row leads with whether a tag inside it read GPC, never which tag; names every cookie written inside it, amber where the count includes the name and secondary where it does not; and says who loaded it in the vendor row's words. Every panel has the same sections in the same order, the Google tag's without the containers it loaded. Requests are companies and domains, never a count.*

## First party (the Overview's last section)

*The cookies charged to the site itself: set by its own responses, or written by scripts it serves from its own domain. One row, closed until opened: the site's registrable domain and every cookie name under it, as a vendor row lists them. Open, a sentence saying which cookies are here and which are listed under a third party, then two lists of names, an empty one reading 'none observed', and the cap note once after both. Nothing in it is counted.*

## Feedback

*Three report paths and the export. The finding path carries page data, always masked; the bug and feature paths carry none, and the copy has to make that legible. The export keeps the same record on the reader's device as three files, each with its own button and a line under it saying what it holds. Only the third, never the primary button, holds cookie values, Cookie and Authorization header values and query strings.*
